test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: At what angle is the arc length half the perimeter of the circle?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The total perimeter (circumference) of a circle corresponds to a complete central angle of 360°.

Since the arc length is exactly half of the total perimeter, the corresponding angle will also be exactly half.

⇒ Required Angle = 360° ÷ 2

⇒ Required Angle = 180°

**∴ The correct answer is 180°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/05e86182890bdfb0f84f424e8bc902a762cbb250b09a0d9e3ee65e20801dd4d8.png] 

**Given:**

Arc length = 1/2 × Perimeter of the circle

**Formula Used:**

Perimeter of a circle = 2πr

Arc length = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

**Calculation:**

⇒ Arc length = 1/2 × 2πr

⇒ Arc length = πr

Equating this to the arc length formula:

⇒ (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr = πr

⇒ θ ÷ 360° = πr ÷ 2πr

⇒ θ ÷ 360° = 1/2

⇒ θ = 1/2 × 360°

⇒ θ = 180°

**∴ The correct answer is 180°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector

The area of a sector with central angle θ is directly proportional to its angle and is given by (θ ÷ 360°) × πr².

Perimeter of a Semicircular Region

While the curved arc length of a semicircle is πr, the total perimeter of a closed semicircular region includes the straight diameter as well, making it πr + 2r.

Quadrant of a Circle

A quadrant represents one-fourth of a circle with a central angle of 90°. Its curved arc length is πr ÷ 2.
